subject: Staggered discount taper and capacity uplift — renewal proposal
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@aegisretail.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal options for Aegis Retail subscription

Hi Dylan / Ben,

Quick note from procurement — our Q3 budget planning is underway and we need to lock in terms for our Redwood subscription. Usage has grown ~2.5x year-over-year and we'll need an additional 40% capacity uplift (more embeddings and dedicated GPUs for batch inference).

Two asks:
- What discount paths do you offer for a stepped renewal (we're open to multi-stage commits)?
- Can you provide some sort of short-term credit/drawdown to cover initial overages during onboarding? Finance needs visibility on worst-case spend for the upcoming fiscal year.

We'd like a simple matrix that shows committed units, effective rate, and any one-time credits so we can circulate internally. If you can, please send a draft we can share with our procurement and finance teams.

Best,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Cloud Platforms
Aegis Retail


From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@aegisretail.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal options for Aegis Retail subscription

Hi Liam — thanks for the details and congrats on the growth.

High-level proposal attached (Aegis_Renewal_Draft_v2.pdf) and a short usage extract (usage-report-q1.csv). Key points: 

- Staggered discount taper: protect your effective unit rate for an initial 9-month window, then reduce the discount in two equal steps over the following 6 months. This gives predictable cost for your fiscal quarter while letting us align unit economics over the renewal year.
- Drawdown credits: one-time onboarding credit of $75k to offset migration and initial overages; we can structure this as a refundable draw that applies to overage invoices for the first 3 billing cycles.
- Commit bump options: three-tier commit schedule (base + 25% uplift, base + 40% uplift, base + 60% uplift) with graduated discounts; the 40% uplift map matches the capacity you described.
- Dedicated capacity can be staged: initial burst pool + dedicated instances after month 2 to minimize idle cost.

Can you confirm whether a 9-month protected window aligns with your finance cadence? If yes, we can finalize the pricing matrix and send an addendum (DocuSign) for signature.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call next week to review the matrix and get procurement's feedback. I'm free Tue/Wed afternoon PST.

Thanks — attaching the draft so you have something to circulate.

--
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Renewals & Expansion
Redwood Inference

Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0187

Dylan — thanks for the quick turnaround and the draft. Two clarifying questions from finance: 

1) For the drawdown credit, are there any conditions that would prevent us from using the credit against overage invoices (e.g., timing or specific product lines)?
2) If we agree to the 40% uplift commit, can you lock the effective rate for at least 9 months and provide an estimate of the blended unit price over 12 months so we can forecast conservatively?

If the answers are straightforward we can prepare an internal approval and get back to you. Otherwise we'll schedule a short call.

Regards,
Procurement Team
Aegis Retail


From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Aegis renewal concessions — need sign-off

Dylan / Monica — quick internal note after reviewing the draft and margin impact:

- Drawdown credit: $75k one-time that applies against any overage invoice within the first 3 billing cycles (no product restriction). That keeps it simple for procurement.
- Protected window: 9 months guaranteed for the 40% uplift. After month 9 we step the discount in two equal steps across months 10–15.
- One-time onboarding credit: I'm proposing we bake in an additional $25k onboarding credit (applied separately from the drawdown) to secure the upgrade.

As we discussed, this is slightly on the generous side for the standard playbook. I need explicit approval from leadership to proceed with the combined $100k of credits (drawdown + onboarding). Approving this will help close the 40% uplift tier and expand our committed footprint.

Can you confirm and I'll route to finance for margin check?

Best,
Ben Carter
Sales Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Final renewal addendum and DocuSign link — Aegis Retail (40% uplift)

Hi Liam / Procurement — thanks for the patience. Following internal alignment, here's what we can finalize today: 

Summary of agreed commercial terms (attached addendum and pricing matrix):

- Commit: 40% uplift over current committed units (committed units defined in Appendix A).
- Protected rate window: 9 months from the renewal effective date where the blended unit price shown in the matrix will be honored.
- Discount taper: months 10–12 = 60% of the initial discount; months 13–15 = 30% of the initial discount. (This creates a gradual alignment back to standard list pricing.)
- Credits: one-time onboarding credit of $25,000 plus a $75,000 drawdown credit. Drawdown credit applies to any overage invoices within the first three billing cycles; no product restrictions.
- Dedicated capacity staging: month 1–2 burst pool, month 3 onward dedicated instances per Appendix B.

Next steps: please review the attached addendum and sign the DocuSign link below to lock the renewal. We can begin onboarding within two weeks of signature and will schedule a kickoff to stage the dedicated capacity.

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/links/Aegis-Renewal-Addendum
Attachments: Aegis_Renewal_Draft_v2.pdf, usage-report-q1.csv

If procurement needs a one-page summary for finance, we've also prepared a two-line blended spend estimate (annualized) — reply and I'll send immediately.

Thanks and looking forward to getting this over the line.
